claims.text: An EMPTY ``fail_to_pass`` is an error, not an empty success: a task with no test that must go from red to green cannot fail, and a measurement that cannot fail is the exact defect ``harness._recall``'s vacuous 1.0 already demonstrated in this repo.
claims.why: The code does not include an explicit check for empty fail_to_pass. The docstring claims it is an error, but the validation code only checks for missing or empty required fields via `not task.get(key)`, which would catch an empty list. However, the docstring's reasoning about vacuous recall is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Delegates to :class:`daedalus.kairos.worktree.GitWorktreeManager` on purpose rather than shelling out to ``git worktree add``: that class places worktrees outside the checkout, refuses an allocation whose path is repo-adjacent, and owns a recursive delete that re-verifies every component before every syscall. Its cleanup is the ONLY delete this module performs; there is no ``shutil.rmtree`` here and there must never be one.
claims.why: The code imports GitWorktreeManager and calls its methods; no shutil.rmtree is present in this chunk.

claims.text: The branch ref that ``git worktree add -b`` writes into the shared ``.git`` is reaped afterwards through the manager's own ``reap_branches``, which deletes only what it allocated in THIS process and only when git itself says another ref already contains the tip.
claims.why: The code calls manager.reap_branches() but the implementation of reap_branches is not in this chunk.

claims.text: This is SWE-bench's "test patch", and it is what makes a before-state measurable at all: the base revision predates the fix, so it also predates the fix's tests -- running a FAIL_TO_PASS node against a bare base checkout would only ever report ``missing``.
claims.why: The claim about SWE-bench and missing status is not verifiable from this chunk; it references external context.

claims.text: Bytes are copied verbatim from git (``git show <rev>:<path>``), never decoded and re-encoded, so line endings and encoding are exactly what the commit holds.
claims.why: The code uses target.write_bytes(proc.stdout) without decoding.

claims.text: Raises ``FileNotFoundError`` if a path does not exist at that revision, and :class:`OverlayEscape` if it would land outside the worktree.
claims.why: The code raises FileNotFoundError if git show fails; OverlayEscape is raised by _safe_join (not shown but assumed).

claims.text: The task's own test files are EXCLUDED, because they are applied separately as the overlay -- if the reference patch carried them too, the "after" run would be testing a tree the candidate path never produces, and the two arms would not be comparable.
claims.why: The code adds exclusion paths via `: (exclude)rel` for each path in exclude.

claims.text: A patch that does not apply is a ``could_not_run``, never a ``not_fixed``: "the change was rejected by git" and "the change did not fix the bug" are different facts about different things.
claims.why: The claim about result classification is not verifiable from this chunk; it references external logic.

claims.text: Immutable (frozen dataclass, tuples not lists) and digested, so "what was measured is what was declared" is checkable by a reader instead of being a claim in a docstring. Everything a result depends on is in here: both node id lists, the RESOLVED base sha (not the ref that was typed), the overlay revision and paths, and the gate configuration.
claims.why: The class is frozen, uses tuples, and has a digest property that includes all fields.

claims.text: Change any node id, the base, the overlay or the timeout and the digest changes, which is what lets :func:`correctness_gate` refuse a task that was verified under one selection and presented under another.
claims.why: The claim about correctness_gate is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Node ids are taken EXACTLY as declared -- deduplicated and ordered for determinism, never expanded, never filtered, and never read from the filesystem. There is deliberately no pattern, glob or directory walk here: a set that could grow to match something a candidate added is not a frozen set, and this function is the only place a set is ever built for an evaluation.
claims.why: The code uses sorted(dict.fromkeys(...)) to deduplicate and order, and does not access filesystem.

observations.what: The solo re-run logic (lines 561-573) iterates over unattributed nodes and re-runs each one individually, but it does not update the statuses for nodes that were not unattributed; it only sets statuses for unattributed nodes after solo run. The returncode rc from the initial batch run is used even if solo runs fail.
validate_task does not check for invalid keys beyond the required ones; it only validates the listed keys.
disposable_worktree catches Exception when reaping branches, which could hide programming errors.
apply_test_overlay uses _safe_join to prevent escape, but the implementation of _safe_join is not in this chunk.
reference_patch uses --no-renames, which may produce a patch that does not apply cleanly if the reference revision renamed files.
apply_patch returns None on success, but the return type is not annotated; the docstring says 'Returns None, or the reason.'
Selection.digest truncates SHA256 to 16 hex characters (64 bits), which is relatively short and could lead to collisions.
_check_selection is declared but its body is not in this chunk; the function is incomplete.
